You asked me, 'Binita, when did you first notice?' Honestly, it was small things. My brother Divyansh used to call me every Sunday from his college hostel. Then it was every other Sunday. Then he'd say, 'Can't talk, I'm at the centre.'
When he came home at Holi, he used words I didn't know. 'Awake ones.' 'Noise people.' He called his old school friends noise people. He'd stopped replying to them.
I asked about his exams. He said he'd dropped two papers because 'the real learning is at the centre now'. When Papa asked a question about the fees, Divyansh said, very calmly, 'Only the guide's word is true. Questions are a test of loyalty. People who ask too many get asked to sit out of the circle.'
Then he told me, gently, that maybe I should give him some space. That family can be a distraction.
That's when I got scared. That's why I'm talking to you.

qa.q: What did Divyansh call his old school friends?
qa.a: He called his old school friends noise people.

qa.q: What was Binita feeling when Divyansh said family can be a distraction?
qa.a: Binita was frightened, seeing Divyansh being pulled away from the people who love him.

qa.q: Which warning signs did Binita spot that a counsellor would recognise?
qa.a: Only one source of truth, questions punished by being made to sit out, dropping studies and old friends, and pressure to distance from family.

qa.q: How might Papa have felt when his question about fees was treated as a loyalty test?
qa.a: Papa may have felt shut out and alarmed, realising ordinary questions were no longer allowed.

grounding: It shows a sibling noticing a brother's secrecy, group jargon, dropped friends and studies, one source of truth, penalties for questions and pressure to cut ties.

I'm Tejas, Vinita didi's younger brother. I'm only writing what I saw, because I don't really know what she's thinking.
In August she started going to the 'wellness collective' after her office hours. By October she'd quit the job. She said the collective needed her full-time and that her boss was 'stuck in the old frequency'.
She keeps her phone locked now, face down. When Mummy calls her name she sometimes doesn't answer, like she's somewhere else.
She stopped seeing Rhea and Sonal. When I asked why, she said the leader told them outside friendships 'drain the energy'.
At dinner last week Papa asked who decides things there. Didi said, 'Our leader sees what we can't. Doubting him is how you fall.' Then she said a girl had been made to clean the hall alone for a month for asking about money.
She said it like it was normal. It didn't sound normal to me.

qa.q: When did Vinita quit her job?
qa.a: By October she'd quit the job.

qa.q: What might Tejas be feeling as he writes this account?
qa.a: Tejas seems worried and unsettled, especially after hearing that a girl was punished for asking about money.

qa.q: What could the family do with what they have noticed?
qa.a: They could stay warm and in contact with Vinita, avoid mocking the group, and speak to a counsellor or helpline about the warning signs.

qa.q: How might Rhea and Sonal experience Vinita's sudden silence?
qa.a: They may feel hurt and confused, not knowing that the group has been pushing Vinita to drop outside friends.

grounding: It shows a brother noticing his sister's secrecy, jargon, lost job and friends, one unquestionable leader, penalties for questions and pressure to cut ties.
